note: The header is legible and gives the 8 money columns above, plus a left-hand category column whose labels (1997 MVE...2013 MVE, 1999-2013 PP, 2007-2013 RE, 2010-2013 SUPPLEMENTAL, TAX LIENS, ROLLBACK TAXES, STR/WATER/SEPTIC/SEWER BETT COMM, STR/WATER/SEPTIC/SEWER INT COMM, STREET/WATER BETTERMENT, SEWER USAGE, GRAND TOTAL) I can read. I am not returning row values because the page is rotated and that rotation was not measured (per the project's own rule for reading a scanned table off a photograph: measure the rotation from the page before banding rows, never guess at it). Concrete evidence: the value 1,690.95 appears once under the FORWARD-column x-position on the "1997 MVE" line, then reappears under the BALANCES-column x-position (x=0.844, far right) on the very next y-band, the one nearest the "1998 MVE" label — i.e. a single row's own figures are landing in two different row-bands because the far-right columns are vertically displaced relative to the near-left label column. That is exactly the row-bleed pattern that requires measuring the page's slope (nearest-neighbor median) before a y-band can be trusted, and I have no way to compute that slope reliably from a flat list of box coordinates without running the correction as code, nor to verify it against this page. Lower on the page it is worse: SEWER USAGE and GRAND TOTAL each show duplicate values landing at nearly the same x (e.g. two different PAYMENTS-column figures, two different TRANSFER-column figures, two different BALANCES-column figures, all within one nominal row-band each), meaning those two rows' figures are interleaved across roughly 3-4 normal row-heights of y instead of one — I cannot tell which of a duplicated pair belongs to SEWER USAGE and which to GRAND TOTAL without guessing. A large number of boxes are also OCR garbage rather than numbers ("len en en", "es en", "canesen", "les es", "en en", stray "$"/"S"/"5" glyphs merged into digit strings), which further blocks confident column assignment for the rows they fall in. Rather than force each figure into a column by eye and risk exactly the kind of confident-but-wrong placement this project has been burned by before, I am reporting the columns and row labels only and withholding the numeric cells.
